findings.reason: The protected Python solution uses binary lifting LCA to find the tree median of start, end, and node for each query. Specifically, it computes lca(start, end), lca(start, node), and lca(end, node), returning the deepest node among the three. This resolves each query in O(log n) time after O(n log n) preprocessing; no candidate is required.

In a tree, the closest projection of a node onto the simple path between start and end is the tree median of the three vertices, which is uniquely identified as the deepest of lca(start, end), lca(start, node), and lca(end, node).

Preprocessing tree depth and binary lifting parent tables takes O(n log n) time and space. Answering m queries takes O(m log n) time, giving overall O((n + m) log n) time and O(n log n) auxiliary space. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts tree parameters n, edges, and query triples [start, end, node], returning a list of length m with closest path vertices.

The approach accurately details tree median properties, LCA depth selection logic, binary lifting parent table construction, and O((n + m) log n) time / O(n log n) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover BFS path reconstruction per query, all-pairs precomputation, RMQ Euler tour, start == end, query node on path, endpoint equality, reversed endpoints, single-node trees, and root independence.

App Python and native Python solutions both use the same binary lifting LCA tree-median algorithm with SHA-256 digests d8f1a3a7d504e2f377abedcd16ed1f567d4a6985e6b73d95920cb4c244df0b89 and bd723a191f3dfe47898e9f96cb9b86d355511428d27a5bebb0bae067d3ce6502. Verified submission remains untouched.
